title: 1936 Prairie's chimneys take their photograph's heights and heavy heads
items: The Thompson/Allerton house at 1936 Prairie: the left chimney over the south flank comes down about 0.9 m to the height its winter photograph shows, and both south chimneys now wear what the photograph draws on them: a stone band, a sunk panel on the taller one, and a heavy corbelled head under a broad stone cap in place of a thin slab.
